BILL NUMBER:  S7288

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the general obligations law, in relation to powers of
attorney for financial and estate planning; and directing the law
revision commission to study the implementation of such powers of
attorney


 PURPOSE OF BILL :
To provide technical amendments to revise Ch.644 '08 in regard to the
execution of powers of attorney, provide further guidance regarding
the use of the gifts rider, clarify which transactions using powers
are excluded from this title and to ensure that language is used in a
consistent way throughout the statute.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS OF BILL :
The process of revoking a power of attorney is clarified in
subdivision 3 of S5-1511 of the General Obligations Law (GOL).
Furthermore, paragraph (e) of subdivision 1 of S5-1513 of the GOL is
revised so that subsequently drafted powers of attorney do not
automatically revoke previously drafted powers. In addition, the
ability of agents to act separately or jointly is also clarified in
paragraph (e) of this section of the GOL.

The definition of a power of attorney is refined in subdivision 10 of
S5-1501 of the GOL, and the language regarding the statutory gifts
rider is now used consistently throughout the statute. The gift making
capacity of a power of attorney without a statutory major gifts rider
is stated as a maximum of $500 each year. The gifts rider's purpose is
further clarified in the heading, certain gift transactions, and
language of section 5-1514 of the GOL.

A new section, 5-1501 C has been added to the GOL, listing the types
of powers that this law does not apply to. Some of the excluded powers
listed in this section include: powers with an interest; a power given
for a business purpose; a power given to a creditor in connection with
a loan or other credit transactions; a power given to facilitate
transfer of stocks, bonds or other asses; a proxy used to exercise
voting or management rights within an entity; a power used by a
governmental subdivision, agency or instrumentality; a power given to
a condominium managing agent; a power contained in a limited liability
company operating agreement, partnership agreement declaration of
trust, declaration or condominium, condominium bylaws, offering plan
or other agreement; a power required by federal or state statute other
than this title; a power used to make health care decisions; a power
authorizing acceptance of service of process; and powers involved in
the disposition of remains.

Further clarification is also provided regarding the effect of divorce
on a power of attorney where one spouse was the principal and the
other was the agent prior to their divorce along with the ability of a
principal, to provide for specific succession rules in the power of
attorney.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Ch.644 '08 provides a comprehensive revision to the power of attorney
laws in New York State. The effective date. of Ch.644 '08 was extended
from March 1, 2009 to September 1, 2009 by Ch.4 '09. After the
effective date of the bill, it became apparent that there was a need
to further clarify the application of the Statutory Gifts Rider and
limit the types of transactions subject to this law.

The technical changes and clarifications made by this bill are
necessary in order to facilitate the transition of the comprehensive
changes to the power of attorney laws made by Ch.644 '08.
 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill, 2010.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Effective 30 days after becoming a law and shall be deemed to have
been in full force and effect on and after September 1, 2009.
Provided, that any statutory short form power of attorney and any
statutory gifts rider executed after August 31, 2009 shall remain
valid as will any revocation of a prior power of attorney that was
delivered to the agent before the effective date of this act.
